question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 2x-4y=2 \\  & -4x+6y=20 \\  & -10x+2y=56\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply.

- **I.** The system is consistent dependent
- **II.** The system is inconsistent
- **III.** The system has a unique solution
question.:question/worked-solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -4 & 2 \\ -4 & 6 & 20 \\ -10 & 2 & 56\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & -4 & 2 \\ -4 & 6 & 20 \\ -10 & 2 & 56\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 24 \\ -10 & 2 & 56\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 24 \\ 0 & -18 & 66\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-9){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 24 \\ 0 & 0 & -150\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y=-150,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

As a result, only statement II is true.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & -4x-3y=6 \\  & -2x+2y=1 \\  & 2x+5y=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply.

- **I.** The system has no solution
- **II.** The system is consistent independent
- **III.** The system is consistent dependent
question.:question/worked-solution:
To classify the system, we first try to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}-4 & -3 & 6 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & -5\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}-4 & -3 & 6 \\ -2 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 5 & -5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 2 & 1 \\ -4 & -3 & 6 \\ 2 & 5 & -5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -7 & 4 \\ 2 & 5 & -5\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -7 & 4 \\ 0 & 7 & -4\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -7 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since any numbers $x$ and $y$ are solutions to the third equation $0x+0y=0$, we can remove this equation from the system. So, the corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-2x+2y=1 \\ -7y=4.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get $y=-\frac{4}{7}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get

$$
-2x+2(-\frac{4}{7})=1\,⟹\,x=-\frac{15}{14}.
$$

 
So, we conclude that the system is consistent independent. 

As a result, only statement II is true.

\{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=0 \\ -2x+3y-3z=5 \\ -x+3y+3z=6\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply.

- **I.** The system is consistent independent
- **II.** The system is inconsistent
- **III.** The system is consistent dependent
question.:question/worked-solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & -3 & 5 \\ -1 & 3 & 3 & 6\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & -3 & 5 \\ -1 & 3 & 3 & 6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(2){R}_{1} \\ & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ -1 & 3 & 3 & 6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(1){R}_{1} \\ & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 & 6\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

The final row corresponds to the equation $0x+0y+0z=-4,$ and this has no solution. Therefore, our system has no solution, and we conclude that the system is inconsistent.

As a result, only statement II is true.
